text:
Maya: heads-up — saw a regression in canary last night. 99p latency spikes + OOM-ish behavior tied to a kernel selector change. telemetry: kernel=v2_swap increases workspace req by ~30% for long seqs, which pushes KV prefill into fragmentation territory. link to traces: https://ci/reports/trace/1748123300

Aj: can you share a short repro or the trace snippet?

Maya: repro (staging):
```bash
./perf-run --model redwood-v3 --batch-split=auto --seqs=64,512,1024 --prefill=on --workload=mix-heavy-long
```

nvprof excerpt: 
```
GPU kernel: matmul_attn_v2  time=42.3ms  workspace=1.9GB
KV prefill allocs: +12 slots, avg slot=128KB, frag-index=0.42
```

Tao: sounds like batcher is grouping long sequences with v2 kernel which has higher workspace peak. that pushes allocator into many small fragments. two options: 1) soften prefill per-request (throttle/cap) 2) reservoir-slicing: split KV reservoir into fast/slow lanes and slice prefill to avoid creating many small slots.

Ranjit: +1 on reservoir-slicing. also we recently changed kernel-score cutoff from 0.6->0.5 which prefers v2 for marginal cases. that explains the regression. propose adding a workspace_penalty term to kernel scoring that is proportional to estimated workspace(batch, kernel).

Aj: quick numbers from a local run where i reduced slab size:
before: reserved=12.0GB, free-chunks=64, frag-index=0.48
after (slab smaller): reserved=9.2GB, free-chunks=120, frag-index=0.55, 99p latency +5%
So naive slab shrink reduces OOMs but increases tail latency.

Maya: telemetry correlation: when frag-index > 0.4 and prefill_rate > 0.6, we see >80% of OOMs. so prefill policy must be frag-aware. simple mitigation: prefill soft-throttle when workspace_util > 0.85 — staging showed 70% reduction in 99p OOMs.

Infra Bot: deploy-bot: started rollout kernel-selector v1.9 to canary at 1748123400 (status: IN_PROGRESS) :rotating_light:

Ranjit: operational plan:
- add `kernel_workspace_penalty` (float) to scorer, default 0.0 -> 0.3 in canary
- add `prefill_soft_cap` per-request (tokens) with hysteresis when pool_util>80%
- implement reservoir-slicing simulator to pick slice sizes and eviction heuristic
- fallback: if predicted fragmentation delta > threshold -> choose decode-path kernel variant

Samir: i'll build a small simulator to estimate fragmentation for reservoir-slicing and prefill caps. ETA EOD. quick idea: maintain reservoir_slices = [fast(20%), warm(30%), cold(50%)], prefill preferentially into fast until fill_ratio, then slice into warm to avoid many tiny slots.

Tao: also consider per-request soft cap that only evicts within that request's allocation budget rather than immediate global eviction — that reduces churn. but we need to ensure fairness across tenants.

Maya: for immediate mitigation can we flip kernel-selector cutoff back and enable prefill_soft_throttle? that should stop the regression while we iterate on scoring and reservoir slicing.

Aj: i'll open a PR with flags + test harness: `prefill_soft_cap`, `reservoir_slice_size`, `kernel_workspace_penalty`, `prefill_hysteresis_ms`. will add unit tests + a soak job mixing seq lengths [64,256,1024] for 1h.

Ranjit: also wire pprof/nvtx into the console dashboard for quick diagnostics on kernel workspace usage per-request. tag me in the PR.

Maya: perfect — tag me too. test plan: A/B canary 10% -> measure 99p latency, OOM rate, frag-index. if OOM delta < -50% and 99p <= +3% accept.

Samir: copied, starting simulator now. will post results + a small csv of simulated frag-index vs slice config by EOD.

Aj: thanks team. I'll also add a short note in runbook about prefilling throttle thresholds and how to rollback. :thumbsup:
